description: Authentication and self-built email verification. next-auth v4 Credentials provider with JWT sessions carrying role; register API; hashed, 24h, single-use verification tokens; Resend verification email (failures logged, not thrown); verify + resend endpoints; brand-themed login/register/verify pages; session helpers used by later gates. Covers tasks.md tasks 3-4. Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: Create src/lib/auth.ts exporting authOptions: CredentialsProvider (authorize: zod-validate email+password, look up User, bcryptjs.compare against passwordHash, return {id,email,role,emailVerified}); session.strategy='jwt'; callbacks.jwt puts id+role on the token; callbacks.session copies id+role onto session.user; pages.signIn='/login'. Use NEXTAUTH_SECRET via src/lib/env.ts.
Create src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts: const handler = NextAuth(authOptions); export { handler as GET, handler as POST }.
Create src/types/next-auth.d.ts augmenting Session['user'] and JWT with id: string and role: 'CUSTOMER'|'ADMIN'. Ensure tsconfig includes it (it does via **/*.ts).
Create src/lib/session.ts: getCurrentUser() (getServerSession(authOptions)), requireUser() (redirect to /login if none), requireAdmin() (redirect/403 if role!=='ADMIN').
Create src/lib/validation.ts with zod schemas: registerSchema, loginSchema, addressSchema, productSchema, orderStatusSchema (reused by later features).

Create src/lib/tokens.ts: createVerificationToken(userId) generates a random raw token (crypto.randomBytes), stores sha256(raw) in VerificationToken with expiresAt = now+24h, returns raw; consumeVerificationToken(raw) hashes+looks up, checks expiry, deletes on success (single-use), returns userId or null.

Create src/lib/email.ts: Resend client from RESEND_API_KEY + EMAIL_FROM; sendEmail({to,subject,html}) and sendVerificationEmail(to, link); ALL wrapped in try/catch that logs and returns a failure result WITHOUT throwing (email failure must never block the caller).

Create src/app/api/auth/register/route.ts (POST): registerSchema validate, reject duplicate email (409), bcryptjs hash, create User (emailVerified null, role CUSTOMER), create a verification token, send verification email with link `${NEXTAUTH_URL}/verify?token=RAW`; respond 'check your email' even if the email send failed (log it).
Create src/app/api/auth/verify/route.ts (GET and POST): consume token; on success set user.emailVerified = now(); return/redirect success; on expired/invalid return an error state the page can show.
Create src/app/api/auth/resend-verification/route.ts (POST): for a given unverified email, issue a new token + email.
Create src/app/providers.tsx ('use client') wrapping children in next-auth SessionProvider; wire it into src/app/layout.tsx around {children}.

Build src/app/(auth)/register/page.tsx and src/app/(auth)/login/page.tsx (client forms, brand-themed with gulf-blue/persian-blue/brand-white; login uses signIn('credentials')); src/app/(auth)/verify/page.tsx reads ?token, calls the verify endpoint, and renders success/expired/invalid with a resend action.
acceptance_criteria: 'npx tsc --noEmit' passes with session.user.role typed via the augmentation.
'npx next lint' clean; 'npx next build' compiles the [...nextauth], register, verify, and resend routes and the three auth pages.
Verification tokens are stored hashed (sha256), expire in 24h, and are single-use (deleted on consume).
Passwords are bcrypt-hashed; no plaintext password is stored.
Email send failures are caught and logged and do not throw out of register/resend.

findings:
DONE. Verification: prisma generate OK, tsc --noEmit clean, next lint clean, next build compiled all four API routes ([...nextauth], register, verify, resend-verification — all ƒ dynamic) and the three auth pages (login/register/verify — static). Integration notes for later features:
- AUTH CONFIG: `import { authOptions } from "@/lib/auth"` (next-auth v4 NextAuthOptions). CredentialsProvider.authorize zod-validates with loginSchema, looks up User by email, bcryptjs.compare against passwordHash, returns {id,email,name,role,emailVerified}. session.strategy='jwt'; jwt callback puts id+role on token; session callback copies id+role onto session.user; pages.signIn='/login'; secret from env.nextAuthSecret.
- ROUTE HANDLER: src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts exports `{ handler as GET, handler as POST }` from `NextAuth(authOptions)`.
- TYPES: src/types/next-auth.d.ts augments Session['user'] with {id:string, role:Role}, next-auth User with {id,role,emailVerified:Date|null}, and JWT with {id,role}. `Role` imported from @/generated/prisma (CUSTOMER|ADMIN). Picked up by tsconfig **/*.ts include.
- SESSION HELPERS: `import { getCurrentUser, requireUser, requireAdmin } from "@/lib/session"`. getCurrentUser() -> CurrentUser|null via getServerSession(authOptions). requireUser() redirects to /login if no session. requireAdmin() redirects to /login if no session OR role!=='ADMIN'. CurrentUser = {id,email,name?,role}. NOTE: requireAdmin currently redirects (not 403) — API handlers that need a 403 JSON should call getCurrentUser() and branch themselves.
- CHECKOUT GATE REMINDER: session helpers expose role but NOT emailVerified. The checkout gate (session AND emailVerified!=null) must re-fetch the user (prisma.user.findUnique) to read emailVerified, since it is not on the JWT/session.
- VALIDATION: `import { registerSchema, loginSchema, addressSchema, productSchema, orderStatusSchema } from "@/lib/validation"` (zod). registerSchema: email(trim/lowercase)+password(min8)+name?. loginSchema: email+password. addressSchema: fullName,phone,street,city,state,country(default 'Nigeria'),postalCode?,isDefault?. productSchema: name,description,dialColor,category(default 'watch'),priceKobo(int positive),stock(int>=0),imageUrl(url),imagePublicId?,isActive?. orderStatusSchema: status enum(7 OrderStatus values)+note?. Inferred types exported (RegisterInput, etc.).
- TOKENS: `import { createVerificationToken, consumeVerificationToken } from "@/lib/tokens"`. createVerificationToken(userId) -> raw hex token (crypto.randomBytes(32)); stores sha256(raw) in VerificationToken.token with expiresAt=now+24h. consumeVerificationToken(raw) -> userId|null; sha256-hashes, looks up by unique token, rejects+deletes if expired, deletes on success (single-use).
- EMAIL: `import { sendEmail, sendVerificationEmail } from "@/lib/email"`. Resend client lazily built from env.resendApiKey, from=env.emailFrom. BOTH wrapped in try/catch — return {ok:true,id}|{ok:false,error}, NEVER throw. Reuse this pattern for order-status notifications in FEAT notify service.
- REGISTER API (POST /api/auth/register): registerSchema validate (400), duplicate email -> 409, bcrypt hash (cost 10), create User (emailVerified null, role CUSTOMER), createVerificationToken, email link `${env.nextAuthUrl}/verify?token=RAW`; responds 201 'check your email' even if email send failed (logged).
- VERIFY API: GET consumes ?token and REDIRECTS to `${env.nextAuthUrl}/verify?status=success|invalid` (for emailed links). POST accepts {token} JSON and returns {status} (used by the client /verify page). On success sets user.emailVerified=now().
- RESEND API (POST /api/auth/resend-verification): {email} zod; only issues a new token+email for an EXISTING, still-unverified user; always returns a generic 200 message (no account enumeration).
- PROVIDERS: src/app/providers.tsx ('use client') wraps children in next-auth SessionProvider; wired into src/app/layout.tsx as <Providers>{children}</Providers>. Client components can use useSession()/signIn()/signOut().
- AUTH PAGES (route group src/app/(auth)/): register (fetches /api/auth/register, shows 'check your email'), login (signIn('credentials',{redirect:false}) then router.push(callbackUrl ?? '/shop')), verify (reads ?token->POST verify, or ?status from the GET redirect; shows success/invalid; invalid state has a resend form). All brand-themed (bg-gulf-blue, bg-persian-blue, text-brand-white). login & verify wrap useSearchParams usage in <Suspense> (required for static prerender).
- DB-touching API routes marked `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` (register/verify/resend) so next build does not need a live DB.
